To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the toxicity of mining effluent was correlated with metal speciation determined by the Ion-Exchange Technique, and that the toxicity of the effluent was also correlated with the total concentration of Cu, Ni and Zn predicted by Windermere Humid Aqueous Model.
the toxicity of complex, multi-metal effluents can not be predicted based solely on the concentration of free metal ions.
The release of mining and municipal effluent into natural waters threatens both human and ecological health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated approach for the assessment of metal toxicity in complex natural waters.
the development of a method that can be used to assess the toxicity of complex metal mixtures in natural waters and effluents.
the development and application of a method to assess metal toxicity in complex, multi-contaminated waters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study suggests that metal speciation, especially the free ion activity, is a useful indicator of toxicity in complex waters.
the present study shows the importance of taking all factors into account when assessing metal toxicity of mining effluent.

the observed toxicity is the result of a combination of the metal concentration, the speciation and the bioavailability of the metals, the nutrient concentrations, the diluent water, the presence of other metals, and the presence and concentration of other toxic compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the WHAM-predicted metal speciation can be used as a tool for the assessment of metal toxicity, but the observed toxicity should be considered as the final result of the interaction among the various factors affecting the aquatic environment.

the toxicity of complex mixtures cannot be assessed by considering only one or two metals and the toxicity of a mixture cannot be assessed by the addition of the toxicities of its constituents, and the results of the present work support this statement.

the use of equilibrium- and kinetics-speciation models in combination with bioassays is a promising approach for assessing the toxicity of metal mixtures, but further work is needed to improve the accuracy of the predictions and to better understand the mechanisms involved. © The Author(s) 2015.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the speciation and bioassay methods are not always in agreement, which may be due to the presence of other metals, the presence of organic ligands that may not be accounted for by the WHAM model, or the use of different algal species in the two methods.

, while metal speciation can provide a reasonable prediction of toxicity in some cases, it should be considered as a tool to be used in conjunction with other methods for assessing metal toxicity, rather than a stand-alone approach.

, in complex multi-metallic systems, the observed toxicity is not only related to the concentration of a single metal, but also to the presence of other metals, nutrients, and the type of diluent water.
